chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Mis'mam Kirdin, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Ten [women] are not permissible for your marriage nor for your intimate relations: your slave woman and her mother; your slave woman and the sister of your slave woman; your slave woman and her aunt (paternal) from breastfeeding; your slave woman and her aunt (maternal) from breastfeeding; your slave woman and her sister from breastfeeding; your slave woman who has breastfed you; your slave woman who has been impregnated until she completes her waiting period with one menstruation; your slave woman who is pregnant by another man; your slave woman who is being sold by a seller; and your slave woman who has a husband and is under his authority.'
ai.seo_question: What are the ten conditions under which a master cannot marry his female slave according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Imam al-Sadiq from Imam Ali, details ten specific prohibitions regarding the marriage of a master to his female slave (uma), emphasizing that kinship through breastfeeding (radha') and existing marital bonds create permanent barriers. It reflects the juristic principle that the rights of the slave owner are limited by these relational constraints, ensuring that marriage is not merely a property transaction but respects established familial ties. The text underscores the ethical treatment of slaves by preventing unions that would create confusing or prohibited degrees of affinity.
